sentences: The detective arrives in the port city at the behest of the American government to help stop an opium smuggling ring.
He receives a warning aboard ship not to stop in the port city.
He is met by his Number One Son, the eldest son, as well as the young man and his fiancée, the young woman.
The detective is the guest of honor at a banquet held that evening, hosted by the dignitary.
When the dignitary opens a box to give a handwritten scroll to the detective, he is shot and killed by a gun inside the booby-trapped box.
The detective meets with the colonel, the commissioner of police, and agrees to investigate the crime.
The next day, American federal bureau man the agent arrives in the port city, accompanied by his valet, the manservant.
That night, an assassin shoots what seems to be a sleeping detective in bed.
But the detective, suspecting another attempt on his life, rigged a dummy and escaped death.
The colonel, the young man, and the young woman try to meet with the agent.
The young man sneaks off and goes through the agent's briefcase, suitcase, and other papers.
The detective arrives, and while he is speaking with the agent is nearly shot.
The detective and the agent managed to retrieve the gun, but the assassin escaped.
A fingerprint on the gun reveals that the young man is the likely suspect, and he is arrested.
A letter the young man had stolen from the agent's things seem innocuous, but the detective takes it as evidence.
The detective returns to his hotel and meets with the eldest son.
They receive a note from Col.
The colonel asking them to come to an office downtown.
They check with police headquarters, which assures them the note is genuine.
The detective goes, but the eldest son realizes the note is fake when Col.
The colonel calls soon thereafter.
The detective is kidnapped and taken into a room to meet with a mysterious Russian.
The eldest son tries to save his father, but is caught.
The two bluff their way out of danger, and after a brief fight manage to escape.
That evening, the detective and the agent meet with Col.
The young woman arrives and asks to see the young man; her request is granted.
But the young woman sneaks the young man a pistol, and the two escape.
Later that day, the agent and the detective return to the house where the detective was held.
The gang has left, but the detective finds an ink pad in the fireplace and takes it as evidence.
The eldest son shows up dressed as a beggar, and the detective sends him home.
Oddly, the detective arrives at the hotel first.
The eldest son shows up later, and reveals that he saw their kidnapper in a taxi on the street and followed him to the nightclub.
Moments later, the agent calls and summons the detective to his apartment.
Before he leaves, the detective sends the eldest son off on a secret mission.
The detective arrives at the agent's apartment, where the federal bureau agent has caught a gangster involved with the smuggling gang.
After a punch to the jaw, the gangster reveals that the nightclub is where the opium gang is hiding out.
The agent calls the police, and asks them to meet them at the club.
The detective and the agent leave for the nightclub.
After the detective and the agent depart, the agent's valet, the manservant, frees the gangster and the two leave.
At the club, the young man (disguised as an able seaman) sees some of the smuggling gang heading toward the basement and follows, but is captured.
The film opens with a trio of explorers in a faraway continent who are hiding in a cave.
One of the explorers, a pregnant woman, is bitten by a vampire bat.
The film then cuts forward in time to a small European village where a series of mysterious murders are taking place.
The villagers readily assemble in mob form, with torches, at the house of the professor (the actor) after every murder.
The villagers suspect that a giant bat is to blame for the murders.
The professor gives the villagers advice on staying safe, and assures them a scientific explanation exists.
However, in subsequent scenes, the professor himself is revealed to be the murderer.
He is seized by attacks (triggered by darkness) which transform him into a trance-like state of murderousness.
After he commits a murder, he awakens from the trance with no memory of the deed, believing himself merely to have fainted.
The professor's obliviousness is further enabled by the intervention of his loyal hunchback the servant, the only person aware of the professor's condition.
The servant follows the professor when he is in his trances, ensuring the professor is not discovered.
An old friend of the professor's, the doctor, arrives to visit, and soon suspects what is happening.

The doctor discloses to the professor that his mother was bitten by a vampire bat, and that traits of vampirism have likely been passed down to him per an old theory of heredity (the audience now understands the pregnant explorer in the opening flashback to have been the professor's mother).
After the professor's fiancé (the actress) is attacked by an entranced professor, the mob of villagers assumes the servant is culpable and chases him to the edge of a cliff inside a cave.
The professor arrives and confesses to the murders, despite the servant's protestations (aimed at saving the professor) that he, the hunchback, is in fact the murderer.
As the mob watches, the professor throws himself over the edge of the cliff and the servant follows.
The story revolves around a series of suspicious fires that have been plaguing the insurance company.
The main character, the investigator, is a former investigator for the company who was fired under questionable circumstances.
However, due to the escalating fire incidents, the company's board of directors is forced to bring the investigator back to solve the case.
The investigator sets his demands high, requesting various perks and a hefty bonus for catching the arsonist.
He begins his investigation by assembling a team of trusted individuals, including his new secretary, the assistant.
The investigator meets a mysterious woman named the stranger, who has been present at several fire scenes.
He becomes suspicious of her and starts to suspect her involvement in the fires.

As the investigator delves deeper into the case, he discovers that the stranger's father, the businessman, was the owner of the glass company, which went out of business after the insurance company refused to pay his daughter the heiress.
The investigator learns that the businessman had a life insurance policy with the insurance company and believes that the stranger is seeking revenge for her father's mistreatment.
The investigator confronts the stranger with his suspicions and tricks her into revealing her true identity as the heiress.
He finds evidence in her possessions that seem to confirm her involvement in the fires.
However, when the partner, the investigator's co-investigator, uncovers the truth that the heiress had died several months ago, the investigator realizes that he has framed an innocent person.
Feeling remorseful, the investigator goes to the authorities and confesses his mistake.
He explains that he was driven by his determination to solve the case and bring the real arsonist to justice.
The partner, disappointed with the investigator's actions, leaves him, believing that the investigator would sacrifice anyone to solve a case.
The investigator, determined to make amends, starts investigating the case anew.
He discovers that the heiress's father is alive and has been orchestrating the fires to seek revenge on the insurance company.
The investigator confronts the heiress's father, who confesses to his crimes.
With the truth exposed, the investigator is able to clear the heiress's name.
In the end, the investigator brings the heiress's father to justice and repairs his relationship with the partner.

The scientist, inventor of a new method by which television signals can be instantaneously sent anywhere in the world, refuses to sell the process to television companies, who then send agents to acquire the invention any way they can.

On the night of his initial broadcast the scientist is mysteriously murdered in the middle of his demonstration and it falls to the police chief to determine who the murderer is from the many suspects present.
The scientist's assistant, the aide, has apparently accepted a bribe of $100,000.00 to be a personal spy for a large industrial company.
The suitor is supposedly an industrial spy on a similar mission, and has apparently gotten in romantic good with the scientist's daughter the young woman.
After the murder, these two are the leading suspects.
One man who is never actually identified keeps trying to sneak into the sealed-off mansion and is repeatedly ejected yelling "I have business here!".
The investigation is knocked sideways for a bit when the aide is found stabbed to death.
But it is revealed that he was the dishonest twin brother of federal bureau investigator the lawman; who appears out of nowhere and frightens all the ladies.
The lawman reveals the scientific method in which the murder was committed, and finds stolen blueprints of the invention in a secret compartment in the guilty party's wallet.
On a short flight to an island off the state's coast, the witness.
The witness gets sick.
When he is found dead upon landing, it appears to be murder to fellow passenger the amateur sleuth, but she has a tough time convincing the local police chief and the coroner.

When she contacts her friend, the inspector, for more information about the deceased, he recognizes the name: the man was a vital witness in a case against a crime syndicate and had a price on his head of $10,000.
He flies from the big city to assist her in investigating the case and protect her from mob retribution.
When he arrives, the pair argue over which of the people aboard the plane is the killer: the filmmaker.

The filmmaker, a famous film-industry director, struggling actress the starlet, who is angling for a part in the filmmaker's next movie, honeymooners the bride and the groom, the old captain, a retired, self-confessed former rum runner, and the two pilots.

The amateur sleuth suspects poisoning – the witness had been given a drink, a cigarette, and even a dose of smelling salts by the amateur sleuth herself – but before this can be confirmed, the body is stolen.

While the inspector questions those involved, the amateur sleuth discovers that the mob boss, the gangster who had offered the reward for the witness's death, has registered at the hotel under a flimsy alias.
When she eavesdrops on his telephone conversation, she learns that he will be leaving an envelope for someone.
She purloins it from the mailbox and finds $10,000 inside.
More murders occur.
The groom is shot and killed just before he can reveal some information to the inspector.
Meanwhile, the amateur sleuth and the inspector learn that the first victim was not the witness, but his bodyguard.
He and the real witness had switched identities.
After the mob boss confronts the amateur sleuth at gunpoint, trussing her up and putting her in the closet, from which she is rescued by the inspector, the mob boss is also found dead.
Although it was staged to look like a suicide, the amateur sleuth notices that the pistol in his hand is not his own.

When an employee complains that the fish in the hotel pond are all dead, the amateur sleuth finds a pack of cigarettes discarded nearby; one of the cigarettes had fallen into the water, poisoning and killing the fish.
With the murder weapon found, all the pieces come together.
The amateur sleuth takes the inspector to see the grieving bride.
She offers the widow a cigarette, then casually mentions where she got it.
When the bride refuses to smoke it, the amateur sleuth tells the inspector that the mob boss's gun must be in the room.
The bride pulls it out and tells them that she will have to kill them both now, but the amateur sleuth manages to distract her, enabling the inspector to disarm her.
It turns out that the honeymooners thought they had been doublecrossed by the mob boss when they did not receive their reward for committing murder, unaware that the amateur sleuth had taken it.
When the groom tried to betray the mob boss in return, he was killed by his employer, and the bride then killed the mob boss.

To celebrate their six-month anniversary, suburban socialites the husband and the wife arrange a wild drinking party with friends, culminating in a stop at the restaurant owned by the restaurant owner.
They are unaware that the restaurant owner is conspiring with the chauffeur, the chauffeur of the party host, to kidnap the host.
The next morning the couple awake hung over to find the host dead from a gunshot through the heart and his wife the hostess missing.
The husband calls his friend, the district attorney to investigate.
The hostess arrives with the first friend, at whose home she had slept.
Because of their excessive drinking, no one can remember anything about what had happened the night before.
As circumstantial evidence mounts against the husband, he calls in hypnotist the professor to help everyone try to recover their memories.
Just as the professor is about to reveal the murderer, he is murdered.
Next to be killed is restaurateur the restaurant owner.
After the husband and the wife eavesdrop on him conferring with an accomplice at his restaurant, the restaurant owner discovers them.
The husband bluffs that he knows about the kidnapping plot and the accomplice murders the restaurant owner.
The couple returns home to find the chauffeur murdered in his quarters.
Friend the second friend responds to a frantic telephone call from the first friend.
The husband and the district attorney arrive, as they had planned with the first friend, moments after the second friend.
The second friend attacks the first friend and knocks him out.
When he regains consciousness the first friend attempts to shoot the second friend but the husband saves him.
After the various spouses arrive, the husband announces he has solved the mystery.
The first friend borrowed money from the host on behalf of the second friend, using a false name.
The second friend altered the check to be for $150,000 instead of $50,000 and the host forced the first friend to reveal he had borrowed the money for the second friend.
The second friend shot the host at the second friend's home and brought his body to the party, where everyone assumed he was just passed out.
The second friend paid the chauffeur to remain quiet, which is why the chauffeur had to kill the professor.
The chauffeur, the restaurant owner's accomplice, killed the restaurant owner after the husband spoke to him about the kidnapping plot.
The second friend then shot the chauffeur.
The district attorney places the second friend under arrest and extracts a pledge from the husband and the wife to quit drinking.
They agree and drink a toast to it.
The young man visits his aunt the matriarch.
The matriarch is upset about his affair with actress the actress.
The matriarch thinks the actress is a social inferior and only after money.
The young man says he plans to marry the actress, and has secured a radio contract for her that will allow her to continue her acting career while living with him in the big city.
However, the actress rejects the young man's proposal, saying she has a movie offer and marriage proposal from the rival suitor.
The young man and the actress argue until the actress calls the rival suitor to accept his proposal.
Immediately after the young man leaves, the actress receives a call back from the other woman, who claims she will be marrying the rival suitor the next day.
The young man goes to a club, where he offers the radio contract to the singer.
The rival suitor and the other woman also come to the club, which upsets the singer because the rival suitor has made unwanted advances to her.
The singer's boyfriend, press agent the publicist, approaches the young man's table at the same time as the rival suitor.
The rival suitor tells the publicist about the young man's failed proposal, and the young man punches the rival suitor in the face.
Hearing a rumor that the rival suitor wants revenge for his humiliation, the singer follows the rival suitor home from the club.
At the same time, the actress visits the rival suitor's home, where she is admitted by a butler who tells her he needs to go out, but she can wait for the rival suitor inside.
The other woman brings home the rival suitor, who has passed out drunk, and leaves him on a couch, not realizing that the actress is in the next room.
Soon after, the rival suitor's butler returns and finds him dead on the couch from a gunshot wound.
The police suspect the actress because she admits to being in the rival suitor's home.
She also previously owned a pistol of the same type used in the murder, although she claims to no longer have it.
The actress tells the young man she went to the rival suitor's to turn down his proposal, because she wants to marry the young man instead.
The rival suitor's butler calls claiming to know who committed the murder.
When the actress goes to meet the butler, he is killed by an unknown shooter, using the same type of gun that killed the rival suitor.
When the matriarch visits the actress and sees how distraught she is, the matriarch decides she is innocent.
The actress believes the gun she used to own was stolen by her former butler, but the matriarch finds the gun in the actress's apartment.
The matriarch removes the gun before police can find it.
The matriarch sets a trap by talking openly about having the gun.
She claims to have located the butler who stole it and says he will be coming to testify about who he sold it to.
The killer is revealed to be the publicist, who was jealous over the rival suitor's advances towards the singer.
As a collector of film-industry memorabilia, the publicist had previously purchased the stolen gun from the actress’s butler, and used it to divert suspicion.
Big-city lawyer and playboy the sleuth is asked by old friend the friend to locate his girlfriend the missing woman, who mysteriously disappeared in the other city a year ago.
The friend cannot stop thinking about her, and he believes she is in the big city.

Along with the admirer, who has romantic designs on him, the sleuth attends a hit stage show that stars a masked actress, the stage star, who vanishes in mid-performance when the friend recognizes her and blurts out the missing woman's name.
The gossip columnist claims to have discovered a vital clue to the mystery, but before he can reveal it, he is shot in the sleuth's suite.
The sleuth is the main suspect, but the inspector does not believe him to be guilty, and he gives the resourceful lawyer the freedom to investigate on his own.
The sleuth negotiates with the gangster to retrieve letters embarrassing to the admirer.
When he gets them (using a bit of blackmail), he is annoyed to discover that they actually belong to a friend of the admirer.
The sleuth is visited by an old flame, the former lover, now wed to a lawyer, the husband.
The husband, it turns out, is searching for the missing woman too; she can provide an alibi for his client, convicted of a murder in the other city.

The sleuth sets up a trap in a bohemian-quarter apartment, pretending to have located the missing stage star there and notifying each of the suspects that she is leaving there to meet him at his suite.
He speculates that those who are innocent will go to his suite while the murderer heads to the apartment to silence the stage star.
The killer indeed turns up, in disguise, putting the sleuth and the admirer in grave danger.
Fortunately, the sleuth and the inspector are able to subdue the culprit.
It is the husband.
It turns out that the former lover had carried on affairs, first with the other-city murder victim, then with his accused killer.
The husband killed one of his wife's lovers and tried to frame the other.
To achieve the latter, he needed to silence the missing woman, unaware that she had fled to avoid testifying.
She hated the convicted man for ruining her father.
With everything wrapped up, the sleuth marries the admirer.
On New Year's Eve, after the detective and the wife return from the eastern city to their home in the western city, the couple are invited to dinner with the wife's aristocratic family.
The wife's distraught cousin tells the wife that her playboy husband has been missing for three days.
The wife's aunt, who disapproves of the detective, asks him to quietly investigate the playboy's disappearance.
The former fiancé, the cousin's former fiancé, informs the detective and the wife that a few days earlier, the playboy offered to leave the cousin if the former fiancé paid him $25,000.
The playboy has been at the nightclub, a seedy Chinese nightclub, having an affair with the singer, the club's star performer.
The singer and one of the club's owners, the club boss, plan to steal the money that the former fiancé will pay the playboy.

The singer's brother tries to extort money from her, but the club boss throws him out, just as the detective and the wife arrive looking for the playboy, who tells the couple that he has no intention of coming back to the cousin.
Later, the former fiancé secretly meets with the playboy and gives him negotiable bonds.
When the playboy briefly returns to the family mansion to retrieve some clothes, the cousin follows him with a gun.
The playboy walks out into the fog and is shot dead.
The former fiancé arrives and finds the cousin standing over the playboy with a gun in her hand.
The lieutenant considers the cousin the prime suspect, and her fragile mental state only reinforces his suspicions.
The cousin insists that she never fired her gun, but her claim cannot be substantiated as the former fiancé threw the gun into the bay, thinking she was guilty.
One night, someone throws a rock with a note attached to it through the detective and the wife's window.
The note reveals that the brother is an ex-convict and the singer's husband.
The lieutenant shows the detective several checks that the playboy gave to the singer, including one for $20,000.
The detective compares the signatures and determines that the $20,000 check was forged.
The detective and the lieutenant find the brother murdered in his hotel room.
The detective later discovers that someone, the upstairs tenant, had bugged the singer's apartment from the apartment above hers.
While the detective is upstairs, the club boss enters the singer's apartment.
The detective pursues the club boss into the basement, but the club boss shoots at the detective and disappears.
The detective then discovers the body of the building's janitor.
The wife identifies the janitor as her father's former gardener.
The lieutenant says someone tried to call the detective from the building just before the janitor was killed.
The detective has the lieutenant gather all the suspects in the upstairs tenant's apartment.
The club boss and the singer confess their plan to use a forged check to steal the playboy's money, but each claims to be innocent of murder.
The former fiancé says that he has not seen the janitor in six years but remembers his long white mustache.
The detective realizes that the former fiancé must be lying, having seen a picture of the janitor taken six years before showing that he then had a short dark mustache.
The detective reveals that the upstairs tenant is actually the former fiancé, who killed the playboy out of revenge for taking the cousin away from him.

He rented the upstairs apartment so that he could eavesdrop on the singer's conversations, intending to climb down into her apartment using a makeshift ladder, kill the playboy and plant incriminating evidence.
The janitor discovered the former fiancé's contraptions while doing repair works and called the detective.
The former fiancé heard the phone call and killed the janitor.

After witnessing the former fiancé kill the playboy outside the family mansion, the brother tried to blackmail the former fiancé, so the former fiancé murdered the brother and threw the note through the detective's window as a diversion.
The former fiancé admits that he had been planning to frame the cousin for the playboy's murder, as he hated her for leaving him.
He draws a gun and threatens to shoot the cousin and then himself.
The partner, the club boss's partner in the club, flings his hat in the former fiancé's face, and the former fiancé is overpowered.

This surprises the wife because the detective was responsible for the partner's brother being sent to prison for bank robbery, but the partner admits that he dislikes his brother and likes his brother's girlfriend.
The detective and the wife leave the western city by train, accompanied by the cousin.
Later, alone with the wife, the detective notices that she is knitting a baby's sock and, to his amazement, realizes that she is pregnant.
The detective takes his wife and twelve children on an outing to a circus after receiving a free pass from one of the owners, the co-owner.
The co-owner wants the detective to find out who is sending him anonymous threatening letters.
Nearly all of the circus workers are suspects since the co-owner is very unpopular.
However, when the detective goes to meet him during the night's performance, he finds the man dead, seemingly killed by a rampaging gorilla who somehow escaped from his cage.

The lieutenant takes charge of the investigation, assisted by the detective and his overzealous eldest son, who also takes the opportunity to (unsuccessfully) romance the young acrobat, the contortionist.
On the detective's advice, the lieutenant lets the circus continue to its next stop, with the trio tagging along.
During the train ride, an attempt is made to murder the detective with a poisonous cobra.
Then someone tries to break into the circus's safe, but nothing is missing.
The lieutenant finds a marriage certificate inside, showing that the co-owner supposedly married the circus wardrobe lady in another country.
However, the co-owner's fiancé the trapeze artist claims that she can prove the co-owner was not in the other country on the day indicated on the certificate.
Before she can prove it, during her act, someone shoots one of the ropes of her trapeze swing and she falls to the ground, seriously injured, but still alive.
A doctor is summoned.
The detective states that the trapeze artist is too badly hurt to move, so the doctor must operate on the spot.
The detective asks everyone to keep quiet and clear the area, so as not to cause a potentially fatal distraction for the medical staff during the delicate operation.
Meanwhile, the detective has noticed a newspaper article about a crime committed at a casino on the day of the co-owner's alleged marriage.
He sends his son to a phone for a description of the crooks involved by the police.
When the son returns, he sees a man slug the policeman guarding the gorilla's cage and letting the ape out again.
He struggles with the man but is knocked out.
The gorilla reaches the tent where the operation is in progress and tries to cause trouble.
The operation is a fake, as is the gorilla.
He is shot to death by policemen masquerading as doctors.
It is revealed to be the snake charmer in a costume, trying to pin a second death on the escaped animal.
He and the co-owner had robbed the casino and hidden out at the circus.
However, they had a falling out over the division of the money, leading to the co-owner's murder.
The wardrobe lady and her brother are also arrested for trying to use a forgery to gain half interest in the circus.
The detective agrees to obtain a lifetime pass to the circus for his family.
He sees the son and the young acrobat having some romance together wondering if any future grandchildren will be able to see the circus, too.
